Definition: contraction for G4610; Silas, a Christian:--Silas.
BiblicalUsage: Silas was a chief man among the brethren at Jerusalem, chosen to carry the council's letter to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. He was seized with Paul at Philippi when the masters saw their gains were gone, and sent away by night to Berea, where he went into the synagogue of the Jews.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Silas is the faithful second man, the one who went to prison with Paul and to Berea in the night, and I hold that the church runs on such men as much as on apostles.
RelatedEvents: Paul and Silas in the Philippian Prison
